output.summary: KEP-2503 proposes a community-maintained process for generating and building rpm and deb Kubernetes packages by moving packaging tooling from kubernetes/release into kubernetes/kubernetes, driven by a single YAML config and a Go app that runs fpm inside a Docker container. The KEP is in status implementable, stage alpha, since 2021-02-17.
output.rationale:
Packaging tooling lives separately from Kubernetes, which the readme says "can cause downstream divergence" and is hard for the community to maintain. Co-locating sources and tooling in kubernetes/kubernetes is meant to tie package versioning to releases, ensure CI and released packages are identical, and allow downstream customization. The readme gives no explicit rationale for the choice of fpm beyond it being the build container base.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

evidence.quote: Today, the tooling used to build kubernetes packages is separate from kubernetes itself. This can cause downstream divergence, and cannot be easily maintained by the kubernetes community as a whole.
The primary goal of this proposal is to simplify the lifecycle management of packaging by co-locating the sources and tooling for generating packages into the kubernetes/kubernetes repository.
Move packaging tools out of kubernetes/release and into kubernetes/kubernetes repository
Build inside a docker container based off [`fpm`](https://github.com/jordansissel/fpm).
